scope: Two follow-up public reads only; facts, no market/portfolio judgment.

market.rule_note: Frozen rule calls for any final TradingView one-minute High >=100 from creation to Dec 31 ET; non-TradingView sources are a conditional fallback at resolution.

google_static_chart_data.observed: Captured ordinary Google Finance page body contains a ds:12 embedded array with 21 six-element date-tagged rows. Each observed row has four unlabeled numeric values, an ISO timestamp, and a final numeric field.
google_static_chart_data.observation_pattern: One row at 16:00 America/New_York (-04:00) on each of 21 trading dates in the requested 1M window; this is daily-granularity-looking data, not one-minute candles.
google_static_chart_data.schema_limit: The captured data block does not label the four numeric positions as Open/Close/High/Low; no OHLC field mapping is asserted. It is not the frozen TradingView resolution source.

findings: The unsuffixed TradingView scanner response supplied one positional row for requested columns name/high/low/open/close: STRC,99.13,97.92,98.26,98.62. The response did not echo column labels or any timestamp, so request-order mapping is not an independent field-definition or historical-candle proof.
The earlier suffixed scanner request returned values for high|1/close|1 and nulls for high|1D/close|1D; this follow-up does not establish why the daily suffix fields were null.

Google Finance embeds dated one-month chart tuples but their numeric OHLC positions are unlabeled in the captured response; no JavaScript, batchexecute or authenticated endpoint was used. The one-month history begins well after the market creation date and is a proxy, not TradingView one-minute proof.
limits: No evidence here establishes whether any qualifying TradingView one-minute candle occurred since market creation.
